atoms.canonical_statement: The phase 3 ACNS0332 trial evaluated whether carboplatin added during radiotherapy and isotretinoin added during maintenance improved event-free survival in children and young adults with high-risk medulloblastoma, with a planned molecular subgroup analysis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: To evaluate therapy intensification with carboplatin as a radiosensitizer and isotretinoin as a proapoptotic agent in children with high-risk medulloblastoma...

atoms.canonical_statement: ACNS0332 was a randomized phase 3 trial conducted from March 2007 through September 2018 at Children's Oncology Group institutions in the United States, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.
Eligible participants were 3 to 21 years old with newly diagnosed high-risk medulloblastoma defined by metastatic disease, diffuse anaplasia, or residual tumor greater than 1.5 cm2.

population.label: Eligible high-risk medulloblastoma population
inclusion_criteria: Metastasis, diffuse anaplasia, or residual disease >1.5 cm2

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary survival analysis included 261 patients who remained eligible after prospective eligibility review plus retrospective central pathology and radiology review.
Of 294 enrolled patients with medulloblastoma, 24 were excluded after retrospective central review, leaving 261 for the primary survival analysis.

concept.text: ACNS0332 trial enrollment and central review

outcome.definition: Central pathology or radiology review found ineligibility

quantitative_result.effect_measure: count excluded after retrospective central review
quantitative_result.original_result_text: Twenty-four additional patients were ineligible based on retrospective central pathologic (n = 14) or central radiologic (n = 10) review.

atoms.canonical_statement: All study arms received 36 Gy craniospinal radiotherapy with a 55.8 Gy posterior fossa boost and weekly vincristine; carboplatin-assigned patients also received carboplatin 35 mg/m2 before radiotherapy for 30 doses.
The carboplatin comparator was the same radiotherapy and vincristine backbone without carboplatin.

exposures.details: Same radiotherapy and vincristine backbone without concurrent carboplatin

atoms.canonical_statement: Maintenance therapy consisted of six cycles of cisplatin, cyclophosphamide, and vincristine; isotretinoin-assigned participants received isotretinoin 80 mg/m2 twice daily on days 15 through 28 for 12 cycles during and after maintenance.
The primary clinical trial endpoint was event-free survival, compared between randomized arms with the log-rank test.
The primary biology endpoint was molecular subgroup classification by DNA methylation array.
Molecular classification was performed retrospectively using Illumina EPIC DNA methylation arrays, with molecular data available for 231 of 261 patients in the primary analysis.
Whole-exome sequencing was performed when sufficient DNA was available, and variants in known medulloblastoma-associated genes were manually curated after MuTect2 processing.

Neurocognitive analyses used co-enrollment on ALTE07C1 with assessments near 9, 30, and 60 months after diagnosis and general linear models adjusted for treatment group, sex, payment method, and age at diagnosis.

The final protocol version dated April 11, 2018 retained factorial assignment to carboplatin during radiotherapy and isotretinoin during maintenance, while noting that randomization to isotretinoin arms C and D had stopped on January 27, 2015.
Across the 261-patient analysis population, 5-year event-free survival was 62.9% (95% CI 55.6% to 70.2%).

atoms.canonical_statement: Across the 261-patient analysis population, 5-year overall survival was 73.4% (95% CI 66.7% to 80.1%).

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors recommend concurrent carboplatin during radiotherapy for pediatric patients with high-risk group 3 medulloblastoma.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: concurrent carboplatin treatment during radiotherapy is recommended for pediatric patients with high-risk group 3 medulloblastoma

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors do not recommend concurrent carboplatin for high-risk WNT, SHH, or group 4 medulloblastoma because the observed benefit was limited to group 3.
The authors conclude that rapid integrated molecular diagnosis is necessary for medulloblastoma risk stratification.
The carboplatin subgroup findings are limited because randomization was not stratified by molecular subgroup, so treatment-arm balance within molecular subgroups occurred by chance.
Only about 5% of analyzed patients had residual disease greater than 1.5 cm2 as a high-risk feature, limiting confidence about outcomes for incomplete resection as an isolated risk factor.
Neurocognitive analyses were based on a small co-enrolled subset and had fewer assessments at later time points, limiting precision and generalizability of those findings.

Central pathology and radiology review was retrospective; the study showed that local staging or diagnosis could misclassify some patients and expose standard-risk patients to unnecessarily intensive therapy.
The survival improvement observed with carboplatin in group 3 came with increased hematologic toxicity during induction, so therapy intensification has a measurable toxicity cost.

The study was funded by the National Cancer Institute through the National Clinical Trials Network and supported by specified NCTN grants plus St Baldrick's Foundation, Sontag Foundation, NIH R01 funding, and The Brain Tumor Charity.
The article reports author financial disclosures including grants, consulting fees, and stock ownership for several authors; no other disclosures were reported.
The main article states that the data sharing statement is in Supplement 3, but Supplement 3 is not present in the audited packet.
